---
title: "08 — Evaluate AI/AN versus comparison adults"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** the same *already-developed* model's weighted AUROC, Brier score, and calibration within AI/AN-alone adults and other identified single-race adults in 2025. Race was not used in model fitting or model selection.

## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Compare model reliability by group

Reports sample sizes and effective survey-weighted sample sizes, which help interpret
uncertainty in smaller groups. Unresolved/multiracial race is not silently assigned to
either comparison.

```{r compare-model-reliability-by-group}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Group-specific performance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Apply identical metric definitions to both primary populations.
# Report the selected-model AUROC gap as a point estimate, not an uncertainty interval.

scored <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025")
selected <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")
primary <- scored[cohort %in% primary_groups & valid_outcome(FMD)]

rows <- list()
index <- 0L

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (family in c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
    for (group in primary_groups) {
        index <- index + 1L
        group_data <- primary[cohort == group]
        rows[[index]] <- data.frame(
            family = family,
            cohort = group,
            weighted_metrics(
                group_data$FMD,
                group_data[[paste0("prob_", family)]],
                group_data$RAW_WEIGHT
            )
        )
    }
}
subgroup_metrics <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(subgroup_metrics, "08_2025_subgroup_metrics")
print(subgroup_metrics)

# The AUROC difference is a point estimate; it is NOT a confidence interval.
selected_metrics <- subgroup_metrics[family == selected$chosen_family]
auc_gap <- selected_metrics[cohort == primary_groups[1], auc] -
    selected_metrics[cohort == primary_groups[2], auc]
cat(sprintf(
    "[SUBGROUP] AI/AN minus comparison AUROC = %.4f (point estimate only)\n",
    auc_gap
))
```


## Compare model gains within each population

**Measures:** the 2025 survey-weighted Brier improvement of the nationally selected model over the **same frozen historical-prevalence baseline** within each population. Raw Brier scores across groups are not directly comparable because FMD prevalence differs. A positive relative gain means the classifier outperformed that reference; it is not a parity or fairness guarantee.

```{r compare-group-brier-skill}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Within-group skill against a fixed reference
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the same frozen historical prevalence in both populations.
# Calculate relative improvement within each group rather than equating raw Brier scores
# across groups.

# Use the one historical prevalence established before the 2025 evaluation.
baseline_probability <- selected$training_prevalence
skill_rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (group in primary_groups) {
    group_data <- primary[cohort == group]
    model_metrics <- weighted_metrics(
        group_data$FMD,
        group_data$selected_probability,
        group_data$RAW_WEIGHT
    )
    baseline_metrics <- weighted_metrics(
        group_data$FMD,
        rep(baseline_probability, nrow(group_data)),
        group_data$RAW_WEIGHT
    )
    skill_rows[[group]] <- data.frame(
        cohort = group,
        selected_family = selected$chosen_family,
        selected_brier = model_metrics$brier,
        frozen_baseline_brier = baseline_metrics$brier,
        relative_brier_reduction = (
            baseline_metrics$brier - model_metrics$brier
        ) / baseline_metrics$brier
    )
}
skill_table <- data.table::rbindlist(skill_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(skill_table, "08_2025_subgroup_baseline_skill")
print(skill_table)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    skill_table,
    ggplot2::aes(x = cohort, y = relative_brier_reduction, fill = cohort)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    atg_scale_fill_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 improvement over a frozen historical baseline",
        subtitle = "Within-group relative Brier reduction for the selected national model",
        x = "Population",
        y = "Relative Brier reduction (larger is better)",
        caption = "Baseline is the single pre-2023 national prevalence estimate, not subgroup prevalence."
    )
show_and_save(plot, "08_2025_subgroup_brier_skill", 10, 5)
```



## Show weighted ROC by group

Displays how the frozen classifiers distinguish respondents reporting FMD from
respondents not reporting it. Curves are thinned for display; the AUROC calculation
itself uses weighted scores.

```{r show-weighted-roc-by-group}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighted ROC display
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Construct weighted ROC coordinates separately for each model and population.
# The reduced display coordinates do not replace the full-score AUROC calculation.

curves <- list()
index <- 0L

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (family in c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
    for (group in primary_groups) {
        index <- index + 1L
        data <- primary[cohort == group]
        points <- weighted_roc(
            data$FMD,
            data[[paste0("prob_", family)]],
            data$RAW_WEIGHT
        )
        points$family <- family
        points$cohort <- group
        curves[[index]] <- points
    }
}
roc_table <- data.table::rbindlist(curves)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(roc_table, "08_2025_roc_plot_points")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    roc_table,
    ggplot2::aes(fpr, tpr, color = family)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(
        slope = 1,
        intercept = 0,
        linetype = "dotted",
        color = atg_palette[["sand"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cohort) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    atg_scale_color_models() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 subgroup discrimination: weighted ROC curves",
        x = "False positive rate",
        y = "True positive rate",
        color = "Model"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "08_2025_subgroup_roc", 10, 5)
```
```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize 2025 ROC curves by model and population
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Each panel represents one trained model.
# Each panel contains both population groups.
#
# This allows direct comparison of discrimination
# between AI/AN-alone and comparison respondents.

roc_plot_data <- data.table::copy(roc_table)

# Establish a consistent model ordering.
roc_plot_data[
    ,
    family := factor(
        family,
        levels = c("logistic", "lasso", "forest"),
        labels = c(
            "Logistic regression",
            "LASSO",
            "Random forest"
        )

]

# Sort ROC coordinates before connecting points.
data.table::setorder(
    roc_plot_data,
    family,

    tpr
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    roc_plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = fpr,
        y = tpr,
        color = cohort,

        group = cohort

) +

    ggplot2::geom_abline(
        slope = 1,
        intercept = 0,
        linetype = "longdash",
        color = atg_palette[["sand"]],
        linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    # Population-specific ROC curves.
    ggplot2::geom_line(
        linewidth = 1.15
    ) +
    # Three panels, one for each model.
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(
        ~family,
        nrow = 1
    ) +
    # Equal scaling for fair visual comparison.
    ggplot2::coord_equal(
        xlim = c(0, 1),
        ylim = c(0, 1),
        expand = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)
    ) +

    ) +
    # Preserve existing population colors.
    atg_scale_color_groups() +

        name = "Population",

        legend.position = "bottom",

        title = "2025 model discrimination by population",
        subtitle = paste(
            "Survey-weighted ROC curves for",
            "three historically trained classifiers"
        ),
        x = "False positive rate",
        y = "True positive rate",
        color = "Population",
        linetype = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "Each panel compares the same model",

show_and_save(

```


## Show calibration across risk levels

Within each group, compares mean predicted FMD risk against the observed survey-weighted
FMD share in ten risk bands. Averages can conceal local under- or overprediction.

```{r show-calibration-across-risk-levels}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calibration within ranked risk bands
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sort records within each group and form approximately equal-count bands.
# The band means use survey weights; the band boundaries themselves are not weighted
# quantiles.

calibration_rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (group in primary_groups) {
    group_data <- data.table::copy(primary[cohort == group])
    data.table::setorderv(group_data, "selected_probability")
    group_data[, risk_decile := pmin(10L, 1L + floor(10 * (seq_len(.N) - 1L) / .N))]
    result <- group_data[, .(
        respondents = .N,
        expected = weighted_mean(selected_probability, RAW_WEIGHT),
        observed = weighted_mean(FMD, RAW_WEIGHT)
    ), by = risk_decile]
    result[, cohort := group]
    calibration_rows[[group]] <- result
}
deciles <- data.table::rbindlist(calibration_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(deciles, "08_2025_risk_deciles")



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize 2025 population-specific risk calibration
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare survey-weighted observed FMD prevalence with
# predicted probabilities across ten within-group risk
# bands for each population.
#
# Points above the diagonal indicate underprediction.
# Points below the diagonal indicate overprediction.
#
# This is descriptive: no survey-design CIs are
# calculated in this visualization.

plot_data <- data.table::copy(deciles)

# Confirm that the calibration values are usable.
stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(plot_data$expected)),
    all(is.finite(plot_data$observed)),
    all(plot_data$expected >= 0 & plot_data$expected <= 1),
    all(plot_data$observed >= 0 & plot_data$observed <= 1)
)

# Order observations within each population.
data.table::setorderv(
    plot_data,
    c("cohort", "expected")
)

# Use matching axes and leave enough room for all points.
# Round upward to the nearest five percentage points.
plot_limit <- max(
    0.60,
    ceiling(
        max(plot_data$expected, plot_data$observed) * 20
    ) / 20
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct the calibration plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = expected,
        y = observed,
        color = cohort,
        group = cohort
    )
) +
    # Perfect calibration reference line.
    ggplot2::geom_abline(
        intercept = 0,
        slope = 1,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["mauve"]],
        linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    # Connect the mean estimates in predicted-risk order.
    ggplot2::geom_line(
        linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        size = 3
    ) +
    # Format the probability axis as percentages.
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, plot_limit, by = 0.10),
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    # Format observed prevalence as percentages.
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, plot_limit, by = 0.10),
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    # Preserve equal proportions on both axes.
    ggplot2::coord_equal(
        xlim = c(0, plot_limit),
        ylim = c(0, plot_limit)
    ) +
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(
        plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(
            size = 8,
            hjust = 0.5,
            margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)
        )
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 observed versus predicted mental distress",
        subtitle = paste(
            "Population-specific calibration of the",
            "historically selected logistic model"
        ),
        x = "Average predicted FMD probability",
        y = "Observed FMD prevalence",
        color = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "Above diagonal = underprediction;",
            "below diagonal = overprediction.",
            "\nRisk bands formed separately by population;",
            "survey-design CIs not shown."
        )
    )

show_and_save(
    plot,
    "08_2025_group_calibration_improved",
    10,
    7
)

```


## Estimate survey-design-aware mean outcomes

Accounts for BRFSS strata and PSU clustering when estimating group FMD prevalence and
mean prediction residuals. These intervals do **not** represent uncertainty intervals
for AUROC differences.

```{r estimate-survey-design-aware-mean-outcomes}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Survey-design mean estimates
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Construct the design before restricting to the outcome-observed primary domain.
# These mean-outcome and residual intervals do not quantify AUROC-gap uncertainty.

check_packages("survey")
options(
    survey.lonely.psu = "adjust",
    survey.adjust.domain.lonely = TRUE
)

# Preserve the survey design across all valid-weight observations BEFORE domain
# restriction.
if (anyNA(scored[, .(STATE, STRAT, PSU, RAW_WEIGHT)])) {
    stop("Missing survey-design identifiers; resolve before survey inference")
}
scored[, stratum_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, sep = "_")]
scored[, psu_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU, sep = "_")]
scored[, selected_residual := selected_probability - FMD]
scored[, cohort_primary := factor(
    ifelse(cohort %in% primary_groups, cohort, NA_character_),
    levels = primary_groups
)]

survey_design <- survey::svydesign(
    ids = ~psu_key,
    strata = ~stratum_key,
    weights = ~RAW_WEIGHT,
    data = as.data.frame(scored),
    nest = TRUE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Audit 2025 singleton strata before survey inference
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Count distinct PSUs in the full scored dataset.
full_strata <- scored[
    ,
    .(
        full_psus = data.table::uniqueN(psu_key)
    ),
    by = stratum_key
]

# Count PSUs after restricting to the primary
# populations with a valid FMD outcome.
domain_strata <- scored[
    cohort %in% primary_groups &
        FMD %in% c(0, 1),
    .(
        domain_psus = data.table::uniqueN(psu_key)
    ),
    by = stratum_key
]

# Compare the full sample with the analysis domain.
singleton_audit <- merge(
    full_strata,
    domain_strata,
    by = "stratum_key",
    all.x = TRUE
)

singleton_audit[
    is.na(domain_psus),
    domain_psus := 0L
]

# Summarize the source of singleton strata.
singleton_summary <- data.table::data.table(
    full_sample_singletons = sum(
        singleton_audit$full_psus == 1L
    ),
    newly_singleton_in_domain = sum(
        singleton_audit$full_psus > 1L &
        singleton_audit$domain_psus == 1L
    ),
    strata_absent_from_domain = sum(
        singleton_audit$domain_psus == 0L
    )
)

print(singleton_summary)

# Retain the audit as a research record.
save_table(
    singleton_summary,
    "08_2025_singleton_summary"
)

primary_design <- subset(
    survey_design,
    !is.na(cohort_primary) & FMD %in% c(0, 1)
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimate subgroup prevalence and summarize PSU warnings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep track of singleton-PSU warnings without flooding
# the console. All other warnings remain visible.
singleton_warnings <- 0L

prevalence <- withCallingHandlers(
    survey::svyby(
        ~FMD,
        ~cohort_primary,
        design = primary_design,
        FUN = survey::svymean,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        vartype = c("se", "ci"),
        # Keep the group covariance so the contrast below has a proper SE.
        covmat = TRUE
    ),
    warning = function(w) {
        message_text <- conditionMessage(w)

        if (grepl(
            "has only one PSU at stage 1",
            message_text,
            fixed = TRUE
        )) {
            singleton_warnings <<- singleton_warnings + 1L

            # Prevent the repetitive warning from printing.
            # This does not change the survey calculations.
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }
    }
)

# Report the warnings in a compact summary.
cat(
    "\nSingleton-PSU warning occurrences:",
    singleton_warnings,
    "\n"
)

# Display the completed survey estimates.
print(prevalence)

# Confirm that estimates and SEs are finite.
stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(stats::coef(prevalence))),
    all(is.finite(survey::SE(prevalence)))
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Validate 2025 survey prevalence estimates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract point estimates and standard errors.
estimates <- as.numeric(stats::coef(prevalence))
standard_errors <- as.numeric(survey::SE(prevalence))

# Verify that all calculated values are finite.
stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(estimates)),
    all(is.finite(standard_errors)),
    all(standard_errors >= 0)
)

cat("\nSurvey prevalence estimates are numerically valid.\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimate subgroup calibration errors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# selected_residual = predicted probability - actual FMD.
#
# Negative values indicate underprediction.
# Positive values indicate overprediction.
#
# Retain the singleton-PSU adjustment while summarizing
# repetitive warnings instead of printing each one.

residual_singleton_warnings <- 0L

residuals <- withCallingHandlers(
    survey::svyby(
        ~selected_residual,
        ~cohort_primary,
        design = primary_design,
        FUN = survey::svymean,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        vartype = c("se", "ci")
    ),
    warning = function(w) {
        message_text <- conditionMessage(w)

        if (grepl(
            "has only one PSU at stage 1",
            message_text,
            fixed = TRUE
        )) {
            residual_singleton_warnings <<-
                residual_singleton_warnings + 1L

            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }
    }
)

cat(
    "\nSingleton-PSU warning occurrences:",
    residual_singleton_warnings,
    "\n"
)

print(residuals)

# Validate calculated estimates and standard errors.
stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(stats::coef(residuals))),
    all(is.finite(survey::SE(residuals)))
)

cat("\nCalibration estimates are numerically valid.\n")


# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(as.data.frame(prevalence), "08_2025_prevalence_survey_ci")
save_table(as.data.frame(residuals), "08_2025_calibration_residual_survey_ci")

# Attempt a prevalence-difference confidence interval without mislabeling AUROC.
coefficient <- ifelse(as.character(prevalence$cohort_primary) == primary_groups[1], 1, -1)
contrast <- tryCatch(
    survey::svycontrast(prevalence, coefficient),
    error = function(error) {
        warning("Survey prevalence contrast unavailable: ", conditionMessage(error))
        NULL
    }
)
if (!is.null(contrast)) {
    save_table(data.frame(
        difference = as.numeric(stats::coef(contrast)),
        standard_error = as.numeric(survey::SE(contrast))
    ), "08_2025_prevalence_difference_ci_components")
    print(contrast)
}
```
